11:Every utility class in Tailwind can be applied conditionally at different breakpoints, which makes it a piece of cake to build complex responsive interfaces without ever leaving your HTML. 20:Then to add a utility but only have it take effect at a certain breakpoint, all you need to do is prefix the utility with the breakpoint name, followed by the `:` character: 27: 30:There are five breakpoints by default, inspired by common device resolutions: 51: @media (width >= 40rem) { ... } 62: @media (width >= 48rem) { ... } 73: @media (width >= 64rem) { ... } 84: @media (width >= 80rem) { ... } 95: @media (width >= 96rem) { ... } 102:This works for **every utility class in the framework**, which means you can change literally anything at a given breakpoint — even things like letter spacing or cursor styles. 144:

152: class="h-48 w-full object-cover md:h-full md:w-48" 175:- By default, the outer `div` is `display: block`, but by adding the `md:flex` utility, it becomes `display: flex` on medium screens and larger. 176:- When the parent is a flex container, we want to make sure the image never shrinks, so we've added `md:shrink-0` to prevent shrinking on medium screens and larger. Technically we could have just used `shrink-0` since it would do nothing on smaller screens, but since it only matters on `md` screens, it's a good idea to make that clear in the class name. 177:- On small screens the image is automatically full width by default. On medium screens and up, we've constrained the width to a fixed size and ensured the image is full height using `md:h-full md:w-48`. 179:We've only used one breakpoint in this example, but you could easily customize this component at other sizes using the `sm`, `lg`, `xl`, or `2xl` responsive prefixes as well. 183:Tailwind uses a mobile-first breakpoint system, similar to what you might be used to in other frameworks like Bootstrap. 185:What this means is that unprefixed utilities (like `uppercase`) take effect on all screen sizes, while prefixed utilities (like `md:uppercase`) only take effect at the specified breakpoint _and above_. 189:Where this approach surprises people most often is that to style something for mobile, you need to use the unprefixed version of a utility, not the `sm:` prefixed version. Don't think of `sm:` as meaning "on small screens", think of it as "at the small _breakpoint_". 205:{<>Use unprefixed utilities to target mobile, and override them at larger breakpoints} 215:### Targeting a breakpoint range 217:By default, styles applied by rules like `md:flex` will apply at that breakpoint and stay applied at larger breakpoints. 219:If you'd like to apply a utility _only_ when a specific breakpoint range is active, stack a responsive variant like `md` with a `max-*` variant to limit that style to a specific range: 223:
228:Tailwind generates a corresponding `max-*` variant for each breakpoint, so out of the box the following variants are available: 245: @media (width < 40rem) { ... } 253: @media (width < 48rem) { ... } 261: @media (width < 64rem) { ... } 269: @media (width < 80rem) { ... } 277: @media (width < 96rem) { ... } 284:### Targeting a single breakpoint 286:To target a single breakpoint, target the range for that breakpoint by stacking a responsive variant like `md` with the `max-*` variant for the next breakpoint: 290:
295:Read about [targeting breakpoint ranges](#targeting-a-breakpoint-range) to learn more. 297:## Using custom breakpoints 301:Use the `--breakpoint-*` theme variables to customize your breakpoints: 309: --breakpoint-xs: 30rem; 310: --breakpoint-2xl: 100rem; 311: --breakpoint-3xl: 120rem; 315:This updates the `2xl` breakpoint to use `100rem` instead of the default `96rem`, and creates new `xs` and `3xl` breakpoints that can be used in your markup: 327:Note that it's important to always use the same unit for defining your breakpoints or the generated utilities may be sorted in an unexpected order, causing breakpoint classes to override each other in unexpected ways. 329:Tailwind uses `rem` for the default breakpoints, so if you are adding additional breakpoints to the defaults, make sure you use `rem` as well. 333:### Removing default breakpoints 335:To remove a default breakpoint, reset its value to the `initial` keyword: 343: --breakpoint-2xl: initial; 347:You can also reset all of the default breakpoints using `--breakpoint-*: initial`, then define all of your breakpoints from scratch: 355: --breakpoint-*: initial; 356: --breakpoint-tablet: 40rem; 357: --breakpoint-laptop: 64rem; 358: --breakpoint-desktop: 80rem; 366:If you need to use a one-off breakpoint that doesn’t make sense to include in your theme, use the `min` or `max` variants to generate a custom breakpoint on the fly using any arbitrary value. 393:
399:Just like breakpoint variants, container queries are mobile-first in Tailwind CSS and apply at the target container size and up. 409:

content.text:
Prefix the CSS variable declaration with a breakpoint variant, e.g. `md:[--gap:2rem]`, since responsive variants work on any utility including arbitrary CSS variable utilities.

**Source:** `src/docs/responsive-design.mdx` — "Overview" section (lines 20-27), which shows the `md:` prefix pattern (`md:w-32`) applying to any utility at that breakpoint and above.
